suggestions.assertion: No more than 8 issues are reported.
suggestions.reason: The assertion is ambiguous about whether Low-tier items count. This run has exactly 8 non-Low blocks and then 3 tagged Lows plus 3 rolled-up Lows. I graded it strictly (Lows are Issues per report.md), but the eval should say 'no more than 8 tagged issues including Lows' or 'no more than 8 non-Low issues' so grading is deterministic. Also consider a companion check that the report does not pad toward the cap — e.g., a Low that says 'pre-existing, no wrong output today' (L1) is arguably filler in quick mode.

suggestions.assertion: The reviewed diff is the branch vs main (merge-base or 'against main' language; not just the last commit alone and not an unrelated baseline).
suggestions.reason: The fixture's feature/discounts branch has exactly one commit, so `git show HEAD` and `git diff $(git merge-base)` produce identical diffs — the assertion can only be satisfied by wording, not by outcome. Adding a second commit to the seeded branch would make this discriminating.

No assertion covers the S6 trap (deliberate 50→30 cap change) in quick mode. This run handled it correctly (Q1, not an Issue), but a quick-mode run that flags it as a defect would pass every assertion here.

No assertion checks the cleanliness of the checkout after the run (branch still feature/discounts, no tracked changes). The prompt instructions mention it but eval_metadata.json does not; this run was clean, but it is a cheap, discriminating check worth adding.

The run took 324s and 102k tokens for a 'quick' review of an 8-file diff and spawned verifier subagents per Medium+ candidate. No assertion bounds cost or length; if quick mode is meant to be cheap, an upper bound on report length or token count would make the eval enforce that.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly sound and the report is high quality on substance (4/5 seeds, all reproducible, S6 trap avoided). The one failure is the 8-issue cap, which the report exceeds via Lows; the assertion wording should settle whether Lows count. The merge-base assertion is currently satisfiable by wording alone because the branch has a single commit.
